Physical Linux camera and microphone acceptance: 1739, 1954, 2542

This file is a human procedure. Generation only reads local files. Nothing in a
generated plan is a hardware result. Keep every case not_run until the listed
observations exist. Do not infer physical identity from a friendly name or a
successful RPC. Keep recordings outside Git; they can contain private sound or
images. Use consenting operators and a reserved bench with no other recordings.

Required matrix and provenance

Use a Raspberry Pi 4 with bcm2835-codec and a supported Qualcomm board with
qcom-iris for 1954. Record board revision, OS/image, kernel, firmware, camera USB
serial or CSI connector, encoder driver and /dev/video node mappings. Jetson
nvv4l2h264enc, software x264enc and native camera H264 do not cover this change.
Use a physical microphone through PipeWire and through native ALSA for 2542,
in separate reserved sessions/boards. Do not disable the user's audio service
to manufacture an ALSA case. Native ALSA must be the Agent's observed backend.
The microphone must have a distinct serial/card identity. Duplicate card IDs
or names without a verified physical mapping cannot establish this result.

The generator requires actual preflight records. Capture device info, camera
list and data sources using the candidate CLI and explicit device selector.
On the board, save uname -a, /etc/os-release, /proc/asound/cards, arecord -l,
the camera's udevadm properties, and udevadm properties for the microphone's
actual /dev/snd/controlC<number>. Record USB serial and physical port separately.
For PipeWire also save pw-dump in the same account/session the Agent uses.
Save the installed Agent /proc/<MainPID>/exe resolved path and sha256sum, its
systemctl ExecStart/start timestamp, and the candidate build's source SHA and
binary hash. A local candidate file alone does not prove what the board runs.
Pin the original relevant source commits in the report: 517ac062d for 1739,
9a474f749 for 1954 and eaecf90e3 for 2542. Save a recovery record describing how
the reserved service configuration and device order will be restored.

Generate a fresh directory for each matrix row:
  python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/linux-media-hardware-rehearsal.py generate INVENTORY_JSON NEW_DIRECTORY
The inventory schema is in that script's docstring. The generated commands.json
contains argument arrays, not shell text to eval. Every command names the
reserved device. The exact shell commands are appended below this procedure.

Preflight on the reserved board and operator workstation

1. Reconfirm serial/physical labels and installed hashes immediately before
   starting. Stop if they differ from inventory. On the workstation:
     cd @PLAN@
   Save the exact CLI commands and UTC start/end times with each observation.
   Run the generated info/cameras/sources/episodes commands separately, redirect
   each to a NEW file. Confirm there is no active recording and no armed campaign
   that could start one. Reserve the service exclusively for this procedure.
   Do not stop or disarm a recording owned by someone else.

2. On the board, run console-capture.sh from a copied plan directory. Its
   commands are read-only and require v4l2-ctl, udevadm, ALSA tools, GStreamer and
   systemd. Capture errors as prerequisites; do not omit missing commands and
   report a pass. Save a full video-node listing and each encoder node's driver:
     v4l2-ctl --list-devices
     v4l2-ctl --device="$ENCODER_NODE" --all --list-formats-out
   ENCODER_NODE must be selected by the operator from the actual driver map.
   For every session snapshot, retain the boot ID, Agent PID/start time and
   current camera stable-ID-to-node mapping. The node can change after replug.
   Re-run udevadm and camera list instead of reusing yesterday's node number.

3. Put a new handwritten challenge '@NONCE@ baseline' in the camera's field of
   view, move it, then show a different challenge in the second half of capture.
   Run on the workstation:
     sh capture-camera.sh baseline
   It captures for 45 seconds through the actual Agent. Exit 124 is the bounded
   capture deadline, not success. Early errors, empty files or a frozen stream
   fail. Save all three baseline files. Decode using the commands in step 8.

1739: actual native contention, shared owner and release

4. On the board, start an owned native capture in a separate foreground terminal
   against the exact camera node observed above. This needs exclusive bench
   access and a native camera that rejects a second streaming consumer:
     timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 90s gst-launch-1.0 -v v4l2src device="$CAMERA_NODE" ! fakesink sync=false
   Save its complete output. Confirm fresh buffers and the actual owning PID,
   start time and /proc/<PID>/fd mapping to the camera. While it remains active,
   a second independent native capture must return EBUSY/resource busy:
     timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 10s v4l2-ctl --device="$CAMERA_NODE" --stream-mmap --stream-count=2 --stream-to=/dev/null
   Save exit/status output. A generic timeout or unsupported format is not
   contention proof. If the driver accepts multiple consumers, this row is
   unavailable; use a physically exclusive camera rather than faking EBUSY.
   Run the generated cameras command while busy, then:
     sh capture-camera.sh busy
   With no shareable owner feed/graph, require an early actionable camera-in-use
   error identifying this node, not camera absence, encoder failure or a hang.
   Save discovery output as well; a busy healthy device must not disappear.
   Let the owned foreground process finish or interrupt its terminal and wait
   for it to exit. Do not kill a saved numeric PID after it may have been reaped.

5. Exercise a real sharing owner. In the Agent's actual PipeWire session, save
   pw-dump and match the physical camera through api.v4l2.path plus udev identity.
   Set PW_CAMERA_SERIAL to that observed node's object.serial, not its reused ID.
   Start a foreground consumer of that node:
     timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 180s gst-launch-1.0 -v pipewiresrc target-object="$PW_CAMERA_SERIAL" ! fakesink sync=false
   Verify real changing physical frames and a held native camera, then repeat
   the independent native EBUSY probe. Keep this owner running. On the
   workstation start shared-a and shared-b in two foreground terminals within
   two seconds of one another:
     sh capture-camera.sh shared-a
     sh capture-camera.sh shared-b
   Show distinct moving challenges before and AFTER shared-a ends at 40 seconds.
   shared-b lasts 80 seconds. Decode both and require the second consumer to
   contain the later physical challenge after the first consumer exits. Save
   Agent logs showing 'camera held by another client, capturing through
   PipeWire', its exact node serial and no fallback native-open success.
   A graph existing without an observed busy native driver is insufficient.

   A genuine application owner publishing /frame.jpg can cover the HTTP sharing
   branch separately. Retain the actual camera-owning PID/start time, same network
   namespace and listening socket, image/jpeg plus X-Captured-At-Unix-Ns headers,
   fresh physical challenges and Agent 'capturing shared JPEG feed from camera
   owner' log. Use only its documented start/stop procedure. Do not insert a
   fabricated JPEG server. If unavailable, mark that physical branch not_run;
   portable shared-HTTP tests remain the evidence for its software behavior.

6. After both Wendy consumers exit, verify their capture/encoder subprocesses
   have gone while the unrelated sharing owner remains healthy. Stop only the
   owner created in step 5, wait for its foreground command, and verify no owned
   camera FDs remain. Run:
     sh capture-camera.sh released
   Require fresh direct capture with a new challenge. Save final fd/process and
   device listings. A surviving owner or encoder prevents cleanup passing.

1954: physical capture/encoder negotiation

7. Complete this independently on BOTH named encoder driver families. Use a
   camera/mode requiring Agent encoding; a native H264 passthrough cannot prove
   negotiation. On the reserved Agent, enable GStreamer diagnostic environment
   through that bench's existing service management procedure:
     GST_DEBUG=GST_CAPS:6,v4l2*:6
     GST_DEBUG_NO_COLOR=1
     GST_DEBUG_FILE=/absolute/private/bench-directory/gst-negotiation.log
   Use a newly created directory writable by the Agent account. Record the
   exact temporary configuration, original environment and restoration steps;
   do not overwrite or remove an existing drop-in. Restart only the reserved
   Agent, then verify /proc/<MainPID>/environ contains these settings and the
   installed executable hash still matches. GStreamer children inherit them.
   Run on the workstation with a fresh moving challenge:
     sh capture-camera.sh encoder
   Save journalctl -u wendy-agent for this exact time range, the live child argv,
   driver/node fd mapping and gst-negotiation.log. Require the production log
   'GStreamer encoder selected' to say v4l2h264enc. Require negotiated FIXED sink
   caps at that encoder and its driver node, not merely advertised caps containing
   both options. Require NV12 on qcom-iris. On bcm2835-codec record the selected
   I420 or NV12 format and prove that the actual driver supports it. I420 is the
   original Pi path; selecting another supported format is not itself a failure. Decode H264 with baseline
   profile and level <= 4.0 at a supported resolution/rate, including Pi 1080p30
   when supported. If another encoder wins selection or no fixed caps were
   retained, leave this row unverified. Do not force success by removing plugins.

   Historical control on the reserved Qualcomm board: build a separate candidate
   from the same source with only encoderSegment's v4l2h264enc input changed from
   format={I420,NV12} to format=I420. Save the exact patch/source and both binary
   hashes. Install it by the bench's usual procedure, repeat the same camera
   request into a separate control directory, and require the actual iris
   negotiation failure before decoded frames. Restore the reviewed candidate,
   verify its installed hash, and repeat the successful capture. A missing
   plugin or dead camera is not a valid control. The old I420 restriction can
   work on the Pi; its purpose there is compatibility, not an expected failure.

8. Decode EVERY successful video file on the workstation with ffmpeg/ffprobe.
   Use a new result directory each time and keep stderr and exit statuses:
     ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_streams -show_format -of json "$VIDEO" > "$NEW_PROBE_JSON"
     ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -i "$VIDEO" -map 0:v:0 -f framemd5 "$NEW_FRAME_MD5"
     ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -i "$VIDEO" -vf fps=1 "$NEW_FRAME_DIRECTORY/frame-%04d.png"
   Require clean decode, expected dimensions, multiple changing decoded frames
   spanning the capture interval and legible newly issued physical challenges.
   Compare the shared-b frames after shared-a's end timestamp. A nonempty encoded
   file, changing encoded-byte hash, or a static screenshot is insufficient.
   Keep generated images outside the repository. For encoder proof also retain
   probe codec/profile/level and the fixed negotiated driver caps from step 7.

2542: microphone identity through real renumbering

9. Save fresh sources-before.json, raw pw-dump or /proc/asound card IDs, arecord -l
   and udev serial/port mapping. Select the same stable source ID from the plan,
   never its numeric alias. Confirm no active recording, then run the generated
   microphone_before command. Retain the returned episode ID/name. Speak the
   fresh nonce and 'before', followed by three separated taps near ONLY this
   microphone while a different microphone hears a different challenge. Record
   at least 12 seconds. Verify the active episode still has that exact ID/name
   with the generated episodes command before running stop_owned_episode_only.
   Since data stop has no episode selector, do not run it if ownership changed.
   Inspect and download this exact sealed episode into a new directory using
   the commands below. Require successful checksum verification and complete
   source status, not a zero-sample or failed capture hidden by RPC success.

10. With no capture active, physically unplug the identified microphone and
    replug it after another reserved microphone, or reboot the reserved board
    with the agreed reversed connection order. Do not rename source records or
    change udev rules to simulate this. Preserve serial and port mapping; if the
    source uses a port-derived identity, keep its port and change only ordering.
    For PipeWire require changed numeric object ID/alias with identical node.name;
    for ALSA require changed card number/alias with identical card ID and PCM
    device. Capture the actual kernel/session evidence and sources-after.json.
    Verify the same stable ID resolves to the same physical serial, then run:
      python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/linux-media-hardware-rehearsal.py check-renumber sources-before.json sources-after.json --source "$STABLE_SOURCE" --backend "$BACKEND"
    Save its output. This only verifies the listing contract. Unchanged numeric
    aliases mean the physical renumber experiment has not happened, not a pass.

11. Run microphone_after using the UNCHANGED stable source ID. Speak a new nonce
    and 'after', followed by five separated taps. Keep the other microphone's
    challenge different. Seal only the matching owned episode and inspect and
    download it as in step 9. Find its audio/<source>/index.jsonl and WAV segments.
    Require matching manifest source ID and index source/timing metadata,
    nonzero recorded samples spanning the challenge, 48000 Hz mono 16-bit PCM,
    verified file hashes and no discontinuity/status failure concealed as success.
    Decode every WAV, inspect samples and listen to the two physical challenges:
      ffprobe -v error -show_streams -of json "$WAV" > "$NEW_WAV_PROBE"
      ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -i "$WAV" -f s16le -acodec pcm_s16le "$NEW_PCM"
      ffmpeg -nostdin -v info -i "$WAV" -af astats=metadata=1:reset=0 -f null - 2> "$NEW_PCM_STATS"
    Record reviewer, exact challenge transcript and tap times. Changed/noisy PCM
    alone cannot prove which microphone supplied it; the distinct physical
    challenges and serial mappings must agree before and after renumbering.

12. Missing-device control: finish the episode, then disconnect ONLY the selected
    physical microphone while the other microphone remains present. Save fresh
    sources and attempt record with the same stable ID in a new owned episode
    name. Require explicit missing-source failure or honest unavailable capture
    with no samples attributed to that ID. It must not silently record the other
    microphone. If an episode was created, seal it only after verifying its ID
    and inspect its failure evidence. Reconnect the original device, reconfirm
    identity and capture a final new challenge. Numeric legacy aliases refer to
    whichever current node owns that number; never expect them to stay stable.

Cleanup and review

13. Wait for all owned foreground capture commands and verify their processes,
    encoder children and camera FDs are gone. Seal only an episode that still
    matches the procedure's returned ID/name. Restore temporary debug settings
    and candidate Agent after any historical control, then verify executable
    hash, service health and original environment. Restore physical cable/order
    according to the recovery record. Do not delete other episodes, stop system
    PipeWire globally, kill unrelated processes or remove an existing drop-in.
    Retain any uncertain state and report it for the bench owner to reconcile.

14. Save sha256sum of every log, listing, decoded output, challenge record and
    episode manifest. Add paths/hashes plus UTC intervals and reviewer to each
    evidence.json case. Report each encoder/audio matrix row separately. Missing
    hardware, unavailable sharing owner, failed native EBUSY reproduction, absent
    fixed encoder caps, unchanged numeric alias or absent cleanup proof stays
    pending. Generation and offline tests never change hardware_execution.
    TOPDON 2770 calibrated 96x96 thermometry is a separate physical acceptance:
    these H264/JPEG/PCM captures do not establish raw temperature calibration.
